claims.text: The initial material is equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen or oxidation resistance that limits high-temperature use.
Pack aluminisation can produce a thin alumina layer on cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The alumina layer produced by pack aluminisation will be continuous and adherent on HfNbTaTiZr.
A continuous alumina scale acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier on the alloy surface.
The alumina scale will impede oxygen ingress into HfNbTaTiZr during exposure at approximately 1000 °C in air for 50–100 hours.
Pack aluminisation and subsequent oxidation exposure will leave the alloy microstructure unaltered.
Aluminised samples will have lower oxidation mass gain than untreated samples after exposure at 1000 °C in an oxygen-rich atmosphere.
Aluminised samples will retain an intact protective scale during the specified high-temperature exposure.
The treated alloy's room-temperature tensile ductility will remain within the original 8–16% performance envelope.
The treated alloy's yield strength at 1000 °C and strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1 will remain within the original 163–530 MPa performance envelope.
Oxidation protection depends on the alumina scale remaining continuous and intact under the specified thermal and mechanical conditions.
Nonuniform coating, extreme thermal cycling, or stresses outside the tested strain-rate range may compromise the protective scale.
